findings.title: Untrusted diagram code can exfiltrate the paid question bank
findings.problem: In the prepare path, trusted code reads the bank and passes all returned question rows—including stems, options, answers, and rationales—to `call("propose", rows)`. That invokes the selected branch's matcher in a browser bundle. The browser is not configured to block outbound network requests, so branch code can send the bank contents to an external server.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor changes `src/diagrams/match.js` to transmit each question received by `proposePairs` using `fetch`. When a maintainer runs the workflow on that branch, the entitled reader account lets the prepare job read the bank and the branch code exfiltrates it, bypassing the paid-content access restriction.
findings.fix: Do not pass protected bank rows to untrusted branch code. Prefer running a trusted matcher; if branch code must run, isolate it with enforced network egress restrictions and pass only the minimum data needed. Add a test proving that branch code cannot make outbound requests or obtain protected question fields.

findings.title: Kaplan sources are presented as verified on a date the code says they were not checked
findings.problem: `KAPLAN_VERIFIED_AT` changes to `2026-10-28`, while the adjacent comment says Kaplan's pages returned HTTP 403 on the re-check and its figures were NOT verified that day. The generated evidence and public source lists therefore claim a verification date the documented process did not establish.
findings.failure_scenario: A student comparing products sees Kaplan prices and features labeled as accessed on October 28, 2026, and reasonably treats them as freshly checked, even though the code says those figures were not verified then.
findings.fix: Keep Kaplan's last verified date unchanged unless a real manual verification was performed. If it was manually checked, update the comment and record evidence of that check before publishing the new date.

assessment: Two release-blocking issues: the diagram prepare job gives untrusted branch code access to the paid question bank, and the comparison content marks Kaplan sources as newly verified despite the code stating they were not verified.
